prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: نتائج الانتخابات حسب الدائرة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "الدائرة" spans 1 col × 2 row; "المرشح أ" spans 2 col × 1 row; "المرشح ب" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "الدائرة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 130px
  col 2: header "المرشح أ › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 3: header "المرشح أ › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 50px
  col 4: header "المرشح ب › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 5: header "المرشح ب › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 50px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 413px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 412px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Publication table of election results by district, comparing candidate A and candidate B vote counts and vote shares in each district.","reading":"Right-to-left: identify the district at the far right, then scan candidate A votes and percentage, then candidate B votes and percentage; compare candidates within each row and compare vote/share columns down the table.","groups":["col 1: row identifier (district)","cols 2–3: candidate A block (votes, percentage)","cols 4–5: candidate B block (votes, percentage)","cols 2 and 4: vote counts, same role and should align","cols 3 and 5: percentages, same role and should align"],"keep_intact":["all vote counts such as 21,340 and 13,905","all percentages such as 41.2% and 8.6%","candidate labels المرشح أ and المرشح ب","unbreakable Arabic words in district names"],"may_wrap":["multi-word district names such as دائرة المفرق الأولى","two-level header labels if necessary, but not numeric data cells"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [110, 79, 72, 79, 72] · table 413×395px · row heights [39, 39, 66, 66, 66, 39, 39, 39] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [108, 80, 72, 80, 72] · table 413×395px · row heights [39, 39, 66, 66, 66, 39, 39, 39] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [104, 79, 74, 79, 74] · table 411×421px · row heights [39, 39, 92, 66, 66, 39, 39, 39] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
